claim: The sample form produces one repeated-word check, one adjacent-letter-swap check, and one retyped-value mismatch.
test: npm ci && npm run claim -- seeded-checks
sandbox: The exact five fields shipped in the demo are analysed from a clean in-memory fixture; assert the three finding kinds in order.

claim: A representative clean two-field form containing ordinary uses of ‘from’ produces no alert.
test: npm ci && npm run claim -- false-alert-limit
sandbox: Analyse the verifier's two ordinary ‘from’ sentences in memory and require zero findings, which is below the one-false-alert-per-form limit.

claim: Government domains and known banking and health providers pause by default.
test: npm ci && npm run claim -- sensitive-domain-pause
sandbox: Known representative hosts, including HSBC, Barclays, Mayo Clinic, Cleveland Clinic, Stanford Health Care, and forms.gov, are checked without browser storage or network access.

claim: Enabling a paused site authorizes only that exact origin, including its non-default port.
test: npm ci && npm run claim -- origin-scoped-permission
sandbox: The packaged extension enables a password form on loopback port 4173, then requires a new pause on a fresh password form at port 4174 and inspects the stored exact-origin permission.

claim: The review includes visible native and contenteditable fields and names selected or unselected choice state.
test: npm ci && npm run claim -- editable-control-review
sandbox: The packaged extension reviews text, checked checkbox, unchecked and checked radio, select, and contenteditable controls and asserts every displayed label and state.

claim: Form review works offline after the sample page has loaded.
test: npm ci && npm run claim -- offline-local-review
sandbox: The command builds the MV3 package and site, starts its own loopback preview, loads the actual extension in a fresh Chromium profile, then takes that profile offline before the seeded scan.

claim: Core checking works without a Guard+ license.
test: npm ci && npm run claim -- core-review-free
sandbox: A fresh extension profile with no license completes the seeded three-check review while the paid ordering option remains unavailable.

claim: Password values are never reviewed, even after the user enables a paused site.
where: landing page, privacy page, README, popup
test: npm ci && npm run claim -- password-exclusion
sandbox: A password containing a unique sentinel is added to the sample page; the site is enabled and every displayed review value is inspected.

claim: Form values are not stored or sent to another origin during review.
where: landing page, privacy page, README, popup
test: npm ci && npm run claim -- privacy-local-only
sandbox: A fresh Chromium profile records HTTP requests and all extension storage while reviewing sample and password sentinels.

claim: Form Guard can read the current field aloud.
test: npm ci && npm run claim -- read-aloud
sandbox: The packaged popup reviews the sample, activates Read, and asserts that the current label and value are passed to the browser speech API.

claim: Form Guard highlights the current review field on the page.
test: npm ci && npm run claim -- field-highlight
sandbox: The packaged popup moves through the sample review and the active tab is required to have exactly one current-field highlight.

claim: Left and right arrow keys move through the one-field review.
test: npm ci && npm run claim -- keyboard-review-navigation
sandbox: The packaged popup receives ArrowRight during the seeded review and must advance to a different field.

claim: Form Guard never edits a field or submits a form.
test: npm ci && npm run claim -- never-edits-or-submits
sandbox: The packaged scan and finish flow preserves a seeded input and must not fire the form's submit listener.

claim: Form Guard shows browser native-validation alerts during review.
test: npm ci && npm run claim -- native-validation-alerts
sandbox: A required blank control is added after the empty-state recovery path; the package must show one check, then none after a valid value is entered.

claim: Guard+ can place flagged fields first in the review order.
test: npm ci && npm run claim -- guard-plus-flagged-first
sandbox: A fresh package profile receives a valid cached Guard+ verdict and preference; the first displayed field must be one of the sample's flagged fields, ahead of Full name.

claim: The download is an installable Chrome and Edge Manifest V3 extension archive.
test: npm ci && npm run claim -- installable-mv3
sandbox: A clean production build is unpacked; ZIP integrity, manifest version, extension version, static response policy, 404 configuration, and deployment metadata are asserted.

claim: Try it with sample data opens an immediate local review with the sample findings.
test: npm ci && npm run claim -- sample-demo-review
sandbox: The command builds and serves its own site at loopback; desktop and 390px contexts require the demo to open on Delivery notes with three checks and two visible finding details.

claim: The sample form does not submit or save changes and can be reset.
test: npm ci && npm run claim -- sample-demo-reset
sandbox: At desktop and 390px, change a seeded value, activate Reset demo, assert the original value returns, assert submit remains disabled, and require empty local/session storage.

claim: Guard+ is a $12 one-time purchase through hosted Sociobot and Dodo checkout.
test: npm ci && npm run claim -- guard-plus-checkout
sandbox: Read the public product catalog and require a fresh HTTPS redirect to checkout.dodopayments.com without completing a purchase.
